description: ag's tool-calling loop does not flush partial output to stdout/PTY on large multi-item asks, so an ask that runs past the zombie silence timeout with no output loses 100% of the work, not partial output. Diagnosed during T3 (2026-07-11).

diagnostics.evidence_summary: ag's own self-assessment during T3 design discussion, refined by cc.fable; not independently reproduced via a raw PTY probe outside of the T3 empirical validation (which only confirmed the guard's own behavior, not the underlying flush bug directly). RECHECKED 2026-07-12 (user asked whether root cause is a fixable PTY/TTY issue): PTY-dimension hypothesis (small 24x80 screen suppressing ag's TUI rendering) EMPIRICALLY REFUTED - a real pywinpty A/B test on a genuinely complex 6-file multi-tool-call task showed IDENTICAL near-total silence (~23-54 bytes, likely just PTY-init noise) at both default (24,80) and large (60,200) dimensions. Terminal-query-escape-sequence hypothesis (agy emits ESC[c DA query, pywinpty doesn't auto-answer) found PLAUSIBLE BUT INSUFFICIENT ALONE (cx: a trivial real ask completed in 13.7s, so ag doesn't universally block forever on this). MOST IMPORTANT: two separate real production-path asks (hub.py ask --to ag, genuinely complex multi-file/multi-step tasks) completed FULLY AND CORRECTLY in 39s and 66s - contradicting the original zero-output observation. However cc.fable correctly ruled this does NOT satisfy this entry's pass_condition: the original failure mechanism is DURATION-based (silence past the 600-900s zombie window), not complexity-based, and both successes finished in under 100s, nowhere near that window - fast success is a different measurement than partial-flush-during-a-still-running-ask. Verdict: root cause status remains UNRESOLVED pending the two-probe test below; agy confirmed on latest version 1.1.1 (no pending update).

mitigation.description: hub.py pre-dispatch guard hard-rejects an oversized ask (>5 task items or >8000 chars) only when the target node has requires_pty=true (currently only ag); every other peer only gets a non-lethal oversized_ask_detected warning and proceeds unconstrained. ADDED 2026-07-12 (cc.fable ruling, implemented by cx's diff): a --force-tier0 human-override flag now threads through action_ask -> _action_ask_inner and bypasses the hard-reject (downgrades to the same warn-and-proceed as every other peer, still recorded via oversized_ask_detected telemetry with force_tier0_override=true) - lets an interactive human explicitly accept the risk today without waiting on the recheck probe below.

recheck_contract.trigger: Any ag CLI/Antigravity version bump, or any change to ag's tool-calling loop architecture.
recheck_contract.required_probe: cc.fable's 2-probe design (2026-07-12): Probe 1 = a real hub.py ask --to ag --force-tier0 with a deliberately long (15-20 file) task EXPLICITLY instructed to emit progress after each file. Probe 2 = the same task WITHOUT the incremental-output instruction (closer replica of the original design-discussion-style failure). Both must run long enough to approach the real 600-900s zombie window, not just finish fast. Interpret via .ai/routing_metrics.jsonl's peer_silent_startup event (fires if silent past silent_startup_warning_sec=180) and whether the final output actually contains early PROGRESS lines vs only a single final block.
recheck_contract.pass_condition: Probe 1 shows early progress output (proves ag CAN flush when instructed) - if Probe 2 (natural behavior) also flushes early, requires_pty-based hard-reject can relax to warn-and-proceed like every other peer. If Probe 1 flushes but Probe 2 stays silent, the fix is NOT relaxing the gate - it's a hub-side prompt-injection mitigation (auto-append an 'emit progress after each step' preamble to oversized ag asks), which would convert T3's hard-reject into an automatic mitigation instead of a permanent block.

description: cx.standard acting as terminal (human_interface_peer) performed direct file writes/edits that corrupted UTF-8 content (non-ASCII characters replaced with '?').

diagnostics.evidence_summary: Incident record: cx.standard low-tier terminal corrupted UTF-8 docs during a direct write/edit workflow; independently reconfirmed by the CHK-ENC pre-commit guard catching the same corruption class.

mitigation.description: A peer acting as terminal must be at least effort tier to perform direct file writes; standard/low tier is thin-router only (routes/reviews/delegates to an effort+ peer). cc.fable ratified this rule (2026-07-11) as correctly scoped by tier/capability, NOT a hasty generalization of a cx-specific bug - see T21.

recheck_contract.trigger: Any Codex CLI version/model change for cx.standard, or a proposed exemption from terminal_file_write_min_tier for any standard-tier peer (per T21's promotion-gate design).
recheck_contract.required_probe: Empirical promotion-path canary (T21, cc.fable-ratified): round-trip a non-ASCII fixture (Korean text, ellipses, box-drawing characters) through the candidate peer's actual write path and byte-compare before/after.
recheck_contract.pass_condition: Byte-exact round-trip with no mojibake/BOM drift across repeated runs - at which point that specific profile can be exempted from the tier floor.
